cells.note: Regulated custody and key-control comparison · United States
cells.detail: Anchorage and BitGo show why legal custody, key control, segregation, wallet policy and movement authorization must be mapped separately from the venue and chain.

cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: The reviewed custody layer remains live and product-specific; no single new September receipt changed the requirement to identify the exact custodian entity, mandate, asset and movement authority.
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: General custody capability is not evidence that Anchorage or BitGo serves a particular tokenized-security route.

cells.text: Access + identity (capability); Post-trade completion (capability); Interoperability + services (support)
items: Access + identity · Wallet + key control: Custody platforms manage keys, approvals and movement controls.
Post-trade completion · Custody, Reconciliation + remedy: Legal custody and reconciliation are post-trade functions; product-specific securities settlement remains separate.
Interoperability + services · API / integration: Custody APIs can attach wallets and settlement instructions to external venues.

cells.text: A custodian's charter or trust status does not make it the issuer, transfer agent, clearing agency, TSV operator or cash-settlement bank for a particular stock pool.
cells.note: Watch: Named product mandate, exact legal entity, asset eligibility, segregation, subcustody, insolvency treatment, settlement instruction and incident receipts.
